A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ViDoRe V3 benchmark. Their main text, tables, figures, equations and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval, answer-generation and visual-grounding evaluations in Section 4, with additional empirical analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations and adds empirical validation of filtering, answer aggregation, query-generation sources and grounding on a high-agreement subset.

M1.justification: The query-generation streams, Qwen2.5-VL-32B pre-filtering and answer aggregation, human verification, translation and evaluated RAG procedures remain unchanged. v2 validates existing components without reporting changes to their operation.

E1.justification: v2 adds pre-filter evaluation on 697 human-annotated query–page pairs from ViDoRe V2 (Table 16), a validation data source not evaluated in v1. The ten ViDoRe V3 corpora, six query languages and three main evaluation tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: New Table 16 compares the chosen Qwen2.5-VL-32B pre-filter against Gemini-2.5-Flash. Although Flash already participated in v1's no-context difficulty assessment, this filtering comparison is new. The main retrieval, reranking, generation and grounding comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Targeted new validation protocols include recall/precision evaluation on 103 positive and 594 negative pairs, GPT-5.2 assessment of aggregated-answer consistency with manual review of divergent cases, and grounding restricted to mean pairwise human IoU of at least 0.7. Existing benchmark evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands validation of benchmark construction: it audits answer aggregation, compares filtering models, examines query-type/format/modality distributions around filtering, analyzes retrieval by query-generation source, and tests grounding on high-agreement pages. These address reliability and bias questions beyond v1's retained regressions, breakdowns and qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Both versions report five independent judge evaluations and five end-to-end pipeline runs, including standard deviations and Krippendorff's alpha (v1 Appendix H; v2 Appendix I). The new analyses introduce no additional repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Substantial new validation results include 86.3% aggregated-answer agreement; filtering recall/precision of 98%/32% for Qwen versus 78%/81% for Gemini; generation-source NDCG means of 0.521, 0.565 and 0.726; filtering distribution statistics; and high-agreement grounding F1 scores of 0.311 and 0.208. Existing main results remain unchanged; the grounding additions use a different subset and are not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The query taxonomy, linear regression formulation and additive performance analysis are retained. No mathematical definitions, derivations or proofs are added or revised. The new IoU threshold defines an empirical evaluation subset.

C1.justification: The abstract's benchmark and performance claims and the introduction's three contributions remain unchanged. The conclusion's cross-lingual wording clarifies existing coverage, while its removed MTEB sentence remains represented by the integration claim in the introduction.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that aggregation predominantly selects or improves human answers, synthetic queries avoid simplicity bias, filtering largely preserves coverage, and grounding remains difficult despite stronger human agreement. These extend discussion of benchmark validity; the existing applicability limitations and principal RAG interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 documents the added checks through the aggregation judge's identity, manual-review procedure, filtering sample composition and grounding subset threshold. This extends reproducibility information, although manual-review and high-agreement subset sizes are unspecified. Existing prompts, model references, hardware disclosures and access information are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning against earlier retrieval and multimodal RAG benchmarks remain unchanged. Replacing multilingual coverage with a cross-lingual setup in the UniDocBench comparison clarifies an already described distinction.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized explanatory additions, a new filtering appendix and generation-source subsection, revised conclusion wording, updated contact information, and moving acknowledgments before detailed contributions. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds six tables: Tables 14, 16–19 and 21. Existing figures and tables are locally repositioned or renumbered, including Figure 7 and Tables 2 and 4. The existing figure set and overall two-column presentation are retained.

improvement.justification: The added audits provide useful evidence about reference-answer fidelity, filtering choices, query-source bias and grounding ambiguity, strengthening support for the benchmark. Unreported manual-review and high-agreement subset sizes, together with broad bias conclusions drawn from limited checks, constrain the gain. The retained main evaluations remain intact.
